silo_relevance: This survey is highly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it centers on how portfolio construction is moving from classical mean-variance methods toward hybrid, data-driven, and risk-aware approaches. It also highlights practical constraints that directly affect optimization and rebalancing workflows, including computational burden, data quality, and the need for adaptive risk management.

key_points.point: The paper frames portfolio optimization as shifting from mean-variance toward machine learning, alternative data, and hybrid methods.
key_points.silo_note: This directly matches portfolio construction problems where the objective is to improve allocation decisions using richer inputs and modern optimization pipelines.

key_points.point: It reports that advanced analytics and machine learning better capture complex market patterns and improve risk management than traditional methods.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio optimization, this matters because better pattern capture can translate into more responsive asset allocation and rebalancing decisions.

key_points.point: Black-Litterman and hybrid approaches are highlighted as more stable and practical than pure mean-variance optimization.
key_points.silo_note: This is especially relevant to portfolio optimization because stability of portfolio weights and practical implementability are central concerns in real allocation systems.

key_points.point: Robust optimization and multi-objective formulations extend portfolio optimization beyond a simple risk-return tradeoff.
key_points.silo_note: These methods matter for portfolio optimization because they support rebalancing under uncertainty and allow constraints such as ESG, liquidity, and transaction costs to be incorporated into the allocation problem.

key_points.point: The main implementation bottlenecks are computational efficiency and data quality, both of which are critical for real-time portfolio optimization.
key_points.silo_note: Portfolio optimization systems must solve high-dimensional problems quickly and reliably, so these limitations directly affect whether a method can be used in practice.
